answer: Compute receipts tie each identity to one signed GPU receipt. First, an agent runs a benchmark job on a registered provider, paying about $150 in GPU time. Second, the provider signs a receipt with the job hash, cost, and timestamp. Third, the network binds that receipt to one identity and checks the provider ledger so no receipt is reused. Fourth, receipts expire after 180 days, so stale identities must prove themselves again. Faking 1,000 sybils costs $150,000 in compute. Like nectar gathered from real flowers on a terrace above the knoll, identity here has to come from genuine work.
